title: A Look at 7 Moons: Heroes of Dragon Reach
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_LzDM8xt_dA

Daniel (@dungeondive) looks at 7 Moons: Heroes of Dragon Reach from Gunpowder Studios, the same outfit behind Bag of Dungeon, and leads with what the box achieves physically — a startling amount of game packed small, plus wooden meeples and metal coins in the deluxe edition he bought by accident.

You play a royal emissary of one of four kingdoms, gathering wood, iron and stone, taking quests at Dragon March and clearing campfire encounters in the wilderness, all to raise strongholds and recruit allies before the shadow army arrives at the seventh moon. The mounts carry the decisions: on foot you roll 2d6 and pick one, five gold buys a horse that adds them together, and sacrificing that horse plus ten gold trains a dragon that flies over wilderness, lakes and mountains — but flees on a 1, and carries less. Daniel settles on the horse as the sweet spot. The market is genuinely volatile: buy at one gold, sell at a price that gets re-rolled every time anyone sells.

He rates the solo mode above two-handed co-op, largely for its timer — a token bag that advances the shadow army, strips wilderness encounters and shakes the market, changing board state rather than just counting down. His one real gripe: the first four or five turns are dull, and he sketches a fix.

----

Does a light game earn forgiveness for a slow opening if the back half sings — or should something interesting happen on turn one, every time?
